solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

B020-01.notes: 16x10^-6 / 2x10^-5 = 8x10^-1 = 0.8. Calculator makes it routine; distractor C/D catch exponent-sign slips.

flags: minor: every choice is a valid b (-25,-14,-11,-10 from factor pairs 1x24,2x12,3x8,4x6), so the item tests 'greatest' of negatives; fine but students choosing -25 by magnitude is the main trap
B020-02.notes: b = -(r1+r2); positive-integer factor pairs of 24 give sums 25,14,11,10; greatest b = -10.

B020-05.notes: Triangles ABE ~ CDE, AE:EC = 6:15, AE = 14*6/21 = 4. Requires similar-triangle insight; D (half) and B (14*6/15) are tempting.

B020-06.notes: h = sqrt(25-9) = 4; V = (1/3)pi*9*4 = 12pi. Trap: using slant height gives 15pi.

flags: Naive linear reasoning (ring width 2 out of radius 6, or 'one of three regions') also gives 1/3, so the most common misconception reaches the key; item does not discriminate area reasoning. Consider radii 1, 3, 6 or asking for the outer ring (20/36 = 5/9).
B020-07.notes: (16pi - 4pi)/36pi = 12/36 = 1/3. Correct and unique, but the naive 'one of three regions' or width-based guess also lands on 1/3.

B020-08.notes: Adding the mean (14) reduces SD (pop 2.83->2.58; sample 3.16->2.83). Adding 10 or 18 increases SD under either definition; 30 increases greatly. Unique.

B020-09.notes: 40+0.25m < 25+0.40m -> m > 100; costs equal at 100, so least whole number is 101. Trap B (equality point).
